note: Gaps between keriox and the KERI specification found in a review of keriox (branch test/keri-spec-vectors). gen_vectors.py writes one or more vectors per gap; `expected` is the specification's outcome, `keripy_expected` what the review expected keripy to do (each vector records what keripy actually does).

gaps.title: Prior-next rotation threshold can be met by one exposed key repeated in k
gaps.spec_quote: To establish verifiable rotation control authority, the current key list MUST include a satisfiable subset of exposed (unblinded) pre-rotated next keys from the most recent prior Establishment event. Where satisfiable concerns the prior next threshold.

gaps.title: An integer threshold of 0 is always met, so nt=0 with a non-empty n lets any key rotate (keripy treats 0 as never met)
gaps.spec_section: Key and key digest threshold fields; Rotation using pre-rotation
gaps.spec_quote: The threshold value MAY be either the simple case of a hex-encoded non-negative integer or the complex case of a list of clauses of fractional weights.

gaps.title: The Establishment-Only (EO) trait is ignored, so ixn is accepted
gaps.spec_quote: The `Establishment-Only`, `EO` config trait enables the Controller to increase its KELs security by not allowing interaction (non-establishment) events. This means all events MUST be signed by first-time, one-time pre-rotated keys. Key compromise is not possible due to repeated exposure of signing keys on [[ref: Interaction event]]s. A Validator MUST invalidate, i.e., drop any non-establishment events.

gaps.title: Do-Not-Delegate (DND) on the delegator is ignored
gaps.spec_quote: A Validator MUST invalidate, i.e., drop any delegated events whose Delegator has this configuration trait.

gaps.title: rot/drt bodies have no c field: spec rotations that carry c are refused, and rotations without c are accepted
gaps.spec_section: Rotation Event Message Body / Delegated Rotation Event Message Body
gaps.spec_quote: The top-level fields of a Rotation, `rot` event message body MUST appear in the following order: `[ v, t, d, i, s, p, kt, k, nt, n, bt, br, ba, c, a]`. All are REQUIRED. No other top-level fields are allowed (MUST NOT appear).

gaps.title: The t field is not bound to the body shape: t=rot with an ixn body is applied as an interaction, and t=dip without di is accepted as an undelegated inception
gaps.spec_section: Interaction / Delegated Inception Event Message Body
gaps.spec_quote: The top-level fields of a Delegated Inception, `dip` event message body MUST appear in the following order: `[ v, t, d, i, s, kt, k, nt, n, bt, b, c, a, di]`. All are REQUIRED. No other top-level fields are allowed (MUST NOT appear).

gaps.title: One invalid controller signature makes the whole event fail, even when the valid ones meet the threshold
gaps.spec_quote: A set of controller-indexed signatures on an interaction or inception event (delegated or not) MUST at least satisfy the current signing threshold in order for that event to be accepted as valid.

gaps.title: Partially signed escrow keeps events and signatures that were never verified, which can block the real event
gaps.spec_quote: A [[ref: Validator]] that receives a key event or non-key-event message that does not have attached at least one verifiable Controller signature MUST drop that message (i.e., not escrow or otherwise accept it).

gaps.title: An identical re-sent event, or one with no verified signature, is recorded as duplicitous, and late signatures are lost
gaps.spec_quote: A duplicitous event is defined as a verified but different version of an event at the same location.

gaps.title: Nested weighted thresholds (weights of weight lists) are not supported
gaps.spec_quote: In a complex fractionally weighted threshold, each weight in a clause MAY be either a simple weight or a weighted list of weights. This provides an additional layer of nesting of weights.

gaps.title: Seal list rejects spec seal types: source {s,d}, latest-est {i}, registrar backer {bi,d}, typed {t,d}
gaps.spec_quote: When a seal appears in a message whose serialization KIND is not CESR native, i.e. is one of JSON, CBOR, or MGPK then it MUST be encoded as a field map in the message's serialization format.

gaps.title: A basic prefix with a non-transferable code is accepted with a non-empty n and can then rotate
gaps.spec_quote: In all cases, the derivation code in the identifier indicates the type of identifier, whether it be a digest of the incepting information (multiple or single keypair) or a single member special case derived from only the public key (both ephemeral or persistent).

gaps.title: Weighted thresholds are not checked for clause sum >= 1 or weight range; unreduced fractions such as "2/4" are refused
gaps.spec_quote: A simple fractionally weighted threshold consists of a list of one or more clauses where each clause is a list of rational fractions (i.e., ratios of non-negative integers expressed as fractions, where zero is not allowed in the denominator).

gaps.title: RB/NRB traits are not enforced, including the required registrar-backer seal
gaps.spec_section: Configuration traits field / Registrar Backer seal
gaps.spec_quote: The `Registrar-Backer`, `RB` config trait indicates that the [[ref: Backer]] (witness) list in the establishment event in which this trait appears provides the AIDs of ledger registrar backers. The event MUST also include Registrar Backer Seal for each registrar backer in the list.

gaps.title: DND (Do-Not-Delegate) config trait of the delegator is ignored; delegated events are accepted
gaps.spec_section: KERI data structures > Configuration traits field
gaps.spec_quote: The `Do-Not-Delegate`, `DND` config trait enables the Controller to limit delegations entirely or limit the depth to which a given AID can delegate. ... A Validator MUST invalidate, i.e., drop any delegated events whose Delegator has this configuration trait.

gaps.title: Delegation escrow releases only one delegated event per delegating event; other delegations anchored by the same event stay stranded
gaps.spec_quote: Because the delegating event payload is a list, a single delegating event may perform multiple delegation operations, one for each delegation seal.

gaps.title: Delegation seal match checks only d; the seal's i and s are ignored
gaps.spec_section: Seals > Key Event seal; KERI key management > Cooperative Delegation
gaps.spec_quote: A delegating event is a type of event that includes in its data payload an event seal of the delegated event that is the target the delegation operation.

gaps.title: A delegated event without a source seal attachment is never matched against an anchor already in the delegator's KEL
gaps.spec_quote: A [[ref: Validator]] MUST be given or find the delegating seal in the delegator’s KEL before the event may be accepted as valid.

gaps.title: Seal model lacks the source, latest-establishment, registrar-backer and typed seals; events carrying them fail SAID checks or fail to parse
gaps.spec_quote: When a seal appears in a message whose serialization KIND is not CESR native, i.e. is one of JSON, CBOR, or MGPK then it MUST be encoded as a field map in the message's serialization format.

gaps.title: A 'dip'-typed event without a di field is accepted as a non-delegated inception (basic prefix)
gaps.spec_section: Key event messages > Delegated Inception Event Message Body
gaps.spec_quote: The top-level fields of a Delegated Inception, `dip` event message body MUST appear in the following order: `[ v, t, d, i, s, kt, k, nt, n, bt, b, c, a, di]`. All are REQUIRED. No other top-level fields are allowed (MUST NOT appear).

gaps.title: A delegating seal in the delegator's icp/dip is refused
gaps.spec_quote: A delegating event is a type of event that includes in its data payload an event seal of the delegated event that is the target the delegation operation.

gaps.title: A SealSourceCouples group with more than one couple makes the delegated event fail to parse
gaps.spec_quote: A given count code can contain multiple seals of the same type.

gaps.title: Duplicate AIDs in the backer list b are accepted
gaps.spec_quote: A given AID MUST NOT appear more than once in any Backer list.

gaps.title: bt != 0 with an empty backer list is not rejected
gaps.spec_quote: When the Backer, `b` field value is an empty list, then the Backer Threshold, bt, field value MUST be `0` (hex-encoded 0).

gaps.title: bt larger than the number of backers is escrowed (and accepted by witnesses) instead of rejected
gaps.spec_quote: The [[ref: Backer]] threshold, `bt` field value is a hex-encoded non-negative integer. This is the number of backers in the backer list that MUST support a key event for it to be valid.

gaps.title: Fractionally weighted bt is accepted although bt must be a hex integer
gaps.spec_quote: The [[ref: Backer]] threshold, `bt` field value is a hex-encoded non-negative integer.

gaps.title: Transferable or non-signing key codes are accepted as witness AIDs
gaps.spec_quote: When the Backers are Witnesses, then the AIDs themselves MUST be non-transferable, fully qualified public keys.

gaps.title: ba entry already in the current witness list is appended again, duplicating it
gaps.spec_quote: Given such an event, the current backer list is updated by appending in order the AIDs from the Backer Add, `ba` list except for any AIDs that already appear in the current Backer list.

gaps.title: Duplicate AIDs inside br or ba are accepted
gaps.spec_section: Backer remove list / Backer add list
gaps.spec_quote: A given AID MUST not appear more than once in any Backer Remove list. ... A given AID MUST NOT appear more than once in any Backer Add list.

gaps.title: br naming a non-witness, or br and ba overlapping: spec silent/ambiguous, keripy rejects, keriox accepts
gaps.spec_section: Backer remove list / Backer add list
gaps.spec_quote: The AIDs in the Backer Remove, `br` list MUST be removed before any AIDs in the Backer Add, `ba` list are appended.

gaps.title: bt=0 with a non-empty backer list: allowed by the spec text, rejected by keripy, accepted by keriox
gaps.spec_quote: The [[ref: Backer]] threshold, `bt` field value is a hex-encoded non-negative integer. This is the number of backers in the backer list that MUST support a key event for it to be valid.

gaps.title: A keriox witness accepts and receipts events of AIDs that do not designate it, without the required witness receipts
gaps.spec_section: Validator Roles and Event Locality; Indexed signatures
gaps.spec_quote: Given a local or remote event, a non-controller, non-witness, non-delegator validator MUST first verify the event's controller signatures, witness signatures (if witnessed), and delegator anchoring seal (if delegated) before it can accept that event into its copy of that event's KEL.

gaps.title: One bad or out-of-range witness signature voids every signature in the same receipt or attachment
gaps.spec_quote: A set of witness-indexed signatures on an interaction, inception, or rotation (delegated or not) for which the effective witness list is not empty MUST satisfy the current witness threshold (of accountable duplicity) for that event to be accepted as valid.

gaps.title: Events at already-used locations are recorded as 'duplicitous' without verification, and verified duplicity is never surfaced
gaps.spec_quote: A duplicitous event is defined as a verified but different version of an event at the same location.

gaps.title: The witness does not distinguish local from remote events before it signs
gaps.spec_quote: Given a remote event, the event's witness SHOULD NOT sign or otherwise accept that event into its copy of that event's KEL. The witness SHOULD NOT propagate that event to other validators including witnesses.

gaps.title: Key state 'ee' has br/ba swapped, and its d is the prior event's SAID after a rotation
gaps.spec_section: Backer remove list / Backer add list (key state notice not defined in spec-body.md)
gaps.spec_quote: Given such an event, the current backer list is updated by removing the AIDs in the Backer Remove, `br` list.

gaps.title: Key state notice writes s and f in decimal but reads them as hex, so no ksn with sn >= 10 can be exchanged
gaps.spec_section: KERI field labels (s: Sequence Number). The spec does not define the /ksn route itself, so this rests on the generic s rule and on keripy interop
gaps.spec_quote: |`s`| Sequence Number | strictly monotonically increasing integer encoded in hex |

gaps.title: BADA accepts an update whose dt equals the prior's dt
gaps.spec_quote:
IF both the Update’s and the Prior's key-states appear at the same location in KEL AND...
        the Update’s date-time is later than the Prior's date-time THEN accept.
  Otherwise, do not accept.

gaps.title: /end/role/cut does not nullify the authorization, and reading it back through the controller panics
gaps.spec_section: RUN off the CRUD / Player EID in Role by CID Nullify Via Cut
gaps.spec_quote: Instead of Delete, Peers Nullify. A Nullify is a special type of Update that indicates that the data in the record is no longer valid but, importantly, without actually erasing or Deleting the record that includes a reference to the latest monotonic determining anchor and/or date-time.

gaps.title: End-role BADA compares against an arbitrary prior keyed by (cid, role) instead of (cid, role, eid)
gaps.spec_section: BADA Rules / OOBI KERI Endpoint Authorization (OKEA)
gaps.spec_quote: The BADA rules apply to any data item stored in a database record whose value is used for some defined purpose.

gaps.title: /loc/scheme nullification with an empty url cannot be parsed
gaps.spec_section: Endpoint Location with Scheme by EID Nullify Via Empty URL
gaps.spec_quote: To Nullify set the `url` to the empty string `""`.

gaps.title: A reply signed with a non-transferable couple is accepted even when the signer prefix has a transferable code
gaps.spec_quote: In this case, the update MUST either includes a reference to the Key-state in the authorizing AID's KEL from which the signing keypair(s) needed to verify the signature is obtained or the AID MUST be ephemeral with a fixed Key-state (has a non-transferable derivation code).

gaps.title: A non-transferable couple whose signature type does not match the key panics the verifier
gaps.spec_quote: Confirm signature on the Update verifies against indicated key-state under which signature was made.

gaps.title: An exn with no sender signatures is accepted and stored in the recipient's mailbox
gaps.spec_quote: Signatures and Seals MUST be attached to the Message body using CESR attachment codes.

gaps.title: The SAID d of qry and exn messages is never verified
gaps.spec_section: Reserved field labels in routed messages
gaps.spec_quote: |`d`| Digest SAID | fully qualified digest of block in which it appears|

gaps.title: The version-string protocol field is not checked to be KERI
gaps.spec_quote: To elaborate, the protocol field, `PPPP` value in the Version String MUST be `KERI` for the KERI protocol.

gaps.title: The pro, bar and xip message types are not supported
gaps.spec_quote: The Routed Messages MUST include a route, `r` field, and MAY include a return route, `rr` field. The value of the route and return route fields are hierarchical. The Routed Message types MUST be as follows `[qry, rpy, pro, bar, xip, exn]`.

gaps.title: The exn body lacks i, ri, x and p, and carries /fwd payloads in a
gaps.spec_section: Exchange Message Body / Prior event SAID field / Exchange identifier field
gaps.spec_quote: The top-level fields of an Exchange, `exn` message body MUST appear in the following order: `[ v, t, d, i, ri, x, p, dt, r, q, a]`. All are REQUIRED. No other top-level fields are allowed (MUST NOT appear).

gaps.title: The spec's qry/rpy/pro/bar field lists omit i, but every example (JSON and native CESR) includes it
gaps.spec_section: Query Message Body / Reply Message Body / Prod / Bare / Native CESR Encodings
gaps.spec_quote: The top-level fields of a Query, `qry` message body MUST appear in the following order: `[ v, t, d, dt, r, rr, q]`. All are REQUIRED. No other top-level fields are allowed (MUST NOT appear).

gaps.title: The key state notice (/ksn) shape is not specified, and keriox and keripy disagree on it
gaps.spec_section: Reply Message Body (the spec defines no ksn / key state notice)
gaps.spec_quote: The top-level fields of a Reply, `rpy` message body MUST appear in the following order: `[ v, t, d, dt, r, a]`. All are REQUIRED.

gaps.title: End-role role values are not enumerated, and keriox and keripy use different sets
gaps.spec_section: OOBI URL (IURL) / OOBI KERI Endpoint Authorization (OKEA)
gaps.spec_quote: The AID may act in any of the KERI roles such as `watcher`, `witness`, `juror`, `judge` or `registrar` but is usually a `controller`.

gaps.title: In the spec's /loc/scheme examples the sender i is the controller, not a.eid, which conflicts with the rule that the EID authorizes its URL
gaps.spec_section: OOBI KERI Endpoint Authorization (OKEA) / Endpoint Location with Scheme by EID Update
gaps.spec_quote: In the other case, an EID authorizes a Loc (URL location) for a scheme.
